players.product: neutral-atom quantum processors (200-qubit QPU hosted at Aramco's Dhahran data center)

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Stéphane Rougeot: revenue for the six months ended June 30, 2026 was EUR 4.9 million versus EUR 4.3 million a year earlier, an increase of approximately 14%; QPU-related services revenue rose EUR 1 million or 34% to EUR 3.9 million, driven primarily by EUR 0.8 million recognized for the QPU upgrade under the Jülich contract; cryostat revenue was EUR 0.9 million versus EUR 1.3 million, reflecting fewer cryostat deliveries (recognized on delivery).
quarterly_data.figure: H1 2026 revenue EUR 4.9 million (+~14% from EUR 4.3 million); QPU-related services EUR 3.9 million (+34%); cryostat revenue EUR 0.9 million

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Wasiq Bokhari and CFO Stéphane Rougeot: as of June 30, 2026 booked and awarded business (order book, firm orders not yet fulfilled) stood at EUR 70.4 million; the CFO said about half is commercial revenue, around EUR 37 million, of which around EUR 12 million is to turn into revenue between now and year-end, and the rest is grants and tax credits recognized as income progressively, some in 2026/2027 and some over longer programs; contract liabilities were EUR 28.2 million versus EUR 23 million at end-2025.
quarterly_data.figure: order book EUR 70.4 million at June 30, 2026 (commercial ~EUR 37 million; ~EUR 12 million to revenue by year-end); contract liabilities EUR 28.2 million

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Stéphane Rougeot: H1 2026 reported operating loss was EUR 59.2 million versus EUR 19.8 million, driven largely by one-off share-based compensation (EUR 27.3 million IFRS 2 charge) and EUR 10.2 million of transaction-related professional fees; excluding these one-offs the operating loss was EUR 21.6 million, a EUR 2.9 million increase like-for-like; net loss was EUR 53.2 million versus EUR 26.1 million.
quarterly_data.figure: operating loss EUR 59.2 million (EUR 21.6 million excluding one-offs); net loss EUR 53.2 million

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Stéphane Rougeot: H1 2026 net cash used in operating activities was EUR 25.2 million (EUR 20 million a year earlier); net cash used in investing was EUR 5 million, including EUR 2 million for property, plant and equipment and EUR 2.4 million for intangible assets; cash and cash equivalents were EUR 110.8 million at end-June 2026 versus EUR 73.8 million at end-2025, with a net liquidity position of EUR 83.8 million.
quarterly_data.figure: operating cash use EUR 25.2 million; PP&E EUR 2 million; cash EUR 110.8 million; net liquidity EUR 83.8 million

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Wasiq Bokhari: Pasqal has seven systems deployed across three continents with three additional systems in production, and believes it operates the world's second-largest fleet of high-complexity quantum computers after IBM; of the seven, a couple are used internally and five are currently externally accessible; CFO Stéphane Rougeot: the systems in production are new, more powerful generations not necessarily contracted with clients and could be produced for cloud availability; the CEO said Pasqal is not experiencing any manufacturing constraints; it operates facilities in France and Canada to build and deliver systems.
quarterly_data.figure: 7 systems deployed (5 externally accessible); 3 in production

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Wasiq Bokhari: Pasqal's public roadmaps share its ability to scale to tens of thousands of high-quality qubits by 2030, progressing toward systems with tens of thousands of physical qubits and hundreds of logical qubits by the end of the decade; asked whether the 2029 target for fault-tolerant quantum computing in the digital domain outlined at its analyst briefing still stands, he said: 'It very much is. It remains our target.'; its current QPUs consume approximately 3.5 kW and are designed to operate inside conventional data center environments.
quarterly_data.figure: fault-tolerant target 2029; tens of thousands of qubits by 2030; ~3.5 kW per QPU

quarterly_data.signal: Customer Crédit Agricole: CEO Wasiq Bokhari said that after multiple years of collaboration in portfolio optimization and credit risk modeling, the relationship has advanced toward production-oriented applications involving capital reserve consumption and risk-weighted assets.

Partner Eleven Ventures: CEO Wasiq Bokhari said that in August Pasqal announced a memorandum of understanding with Eleven Ventures to establish a commercial joint venture intended to deploy, commercialize and scale Pasqal systems across Saudi Arabia and the broader region; the parties have not yet entered a definitive agreement.

Partner USA Rare Earth: CEO Wasiq Bokhari said Pasqal's work with USA Rare Earth builds on its magnetic-material simulation approach plus graph machine learning and other algorithms, with the purpose of improving the efficiency of the rare-earth separation process.

CEO Wasiq Bokhari: Pasqal says it demonstrated an example of quantum advantage in material simulation - a one-to-one simulation of the rare-earth magnetic material TMGO with consistent results across five independently deployed QPUs, predicting new properties that were verified experimentally, in hours versus weeks on classical GPUs; it also demonstrated under live conditions an initial capability to construct and operate key building blocks of the logical qubit, used to solve differential equations.
quarterly_data.figure: five independently deployed QPUs; hours versus weeks on GPUs

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Wasiq Bokhari: through Aeponyx, acquired 18 months ago, Pasqal trapped four individual rubidium atoms using optical tweezers generated by a photonic integrated circuit, which it believes is a first for a neutral-atom quantum computer, with atom lifetimes matching its bulk-optic systems; this gives a roadmap to reduce the optical footprint of future processors by up to 50x, and PICs are to play a role in going beyond tens of thousands of physical qubits per quantum computer.
quarterly_data.figure: four rubidium atoms trapped with PIC tweezers; optical footprint reduction up to 50x

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Stéphane Rougeot: Pasqal has two revenue models - machine sales, recognized at client reception when ownership transfers (back-ended to commissioning), and a cloud-based business selling QPU hours, sometimes packaged with consulting, which is more front-ended and grows with use cases; CEO Wasiq Bokhari: cloud utilization is driven primarily by enterprises, and Pasqal's priority verticals are energy, financial services and high-value materials.

connects_to.relationship: Pasqal 200-qubit neutral-atom QPU and QCaaS platform hosted at Aramco's Dhahran data center; Aramco is a named Pasqal customer

contracts.signal: CEO Wasiq Bokhari: in May Pasqal commissioned the QPU under its Aramco contract, moving the system into its operational phase; the work spans potential applications including reservoir simulation, well placement optimization, rig scheduling and demurrage prediction, and as the relationship has deepened the number of use cases and opportunities has expanded; asked about the multiplier at customers such as Aramco, he said that, just indicatively, use cases can go from one to two to well over a dozen, 'more than a 6x or so increase'; CFO Stéphane Rougeot: revenue for the related service is expected to be recognized in future periods as the services are performed.
